title: Recipient List (v1)
description:
One published version of the Recipient List: the organisations that receive what the fees account passes on, each assigned to one of the movement's seven published categories (ops decision D33, 2026-09-06).

WHAT IT IS. What is passed on goes DIRECTLY, from the fees account, to the public-benefit organisations on this list, in the shares the published allocation rule produces for the month. There is no intermediary: no umbrella, no pooled fund, no earmark instruction, no handling fee. The list names ten to fifteen established organisations anywhere in the world — a removal for cause takes effect at once and may leave a version briefly outside that range, which is why this schema states the range rather than enforcing it: a contract that cannot express the true state is worse than none.

THE LEGAL INSTRUMENT IS THE ANNEX, NOT THIS FILE. The list is the published, versioned annex to the statutes, adopted by the founding assembly; this artifact is its machine-readable form, which is why `x-psn.authoritative` is false. Where the two disagree the annex governs and the divergence is a defect to report.

CHANGES ARE PROSPECTIVE. An addition or a removal takes effect for months AFTER thirty days' public notice (`noticeGivenAt`, `effectiveFrom`). A removal for cause — a sanctions hit, loss of registration, failure to report — takes effect at once, is published with its ground, and the removed recipient's share for that month goes to the other recipients of its category (D33 item 3). Every addition passes the Recipient Standard and is a board decision, minuted and published; no recipient is ever added by free text or by a payer's or a contributor's nomination alone.

THE RECIPIENT STANDARD IS PARTLY MECHANICAL HERE (D33 item 2, whose minimum is constitutional and may only be tightened). Three of its limbs are enforced by this schema rather than described: at least three years of published accounts that are independently audited or officially filed (`standard.accountsYears`), payment by bank transfer only and never in cash or crypto-assets (`standard.bankTransferOnly`), and a published address and website (both required). The rest — lawful foreign receipt under the recipient's own law, screening against the SECO, EU, UN and OFAC lists before listing and before every transfer, independence from every officer and contributor of the Association, the grant letter and the annual use-of-funds statement — travel as required references, because a validator can prove that the evidence was recorded and only a human can prove that it is true.

NO REAL ORGANISATION IS NAMED BEFORE THE OPERATOR ADOPTS THE LIST. A sample dataset marks every entry `sample: true` and its names say so; nothing renders a recipient as listed on the strength of a fixture.

x-psn.phase: P-M3 (producer). No list has been adopted: the first ten to fifteen organisations are named at the founding assembly and published as the statutes' annex, and no transfer is made before an adopted list is published.
x-psn.artifactPath: no path in the FS-00 §6.2 catalogue yet — deliberately deferred; the list is the published, versioned annex to the statutes and is rendered on the causes and transparency pages. The published path is fixed when FS-00 §6.2 adopts this artifact.
x-psn.producer: the operator, from the recipient files, on a board decision that is minuted and published · P-M3: the `recipients` table, published by `jobs.ledger-publish`
consumers: cost-support.v1 transfers and ledger `disburse` rows, which resolve their `recipientId` against the version in force
fsRefs: FS-07 amendment banner (D33 items 1–3 — the `recipients` table at P-M3)

version.description: This list version's own published token — the version cited by every month that transferred under it (URS TRN-024 publishes the Recipient List version in force). The token shape follows `scheduleVersion`, the contract set's other published version on a money-bearing reference (URS ENG-084), so a reader meets one form rather than two.

status.description: `adopted` means this version was adopted by the members and published as the annex to the statutes; `draft` means it was not, and no transfer is ever made against a draft. The distinction is in the artifact because the honesty rule needs it in the artifact: a page cannot tell an adopted list from a proposal by looking at the recipients.

effectiveFrom.description: The first month this version governs. Changes are prospective: a version that adds or removes a recipient takes effect for months after thirty days' public notice (D33 item 3). A removal for cause is the one immediate change, and its recipient carries `removedAt` and `removalGround`.

noticeGivenAt.description: When the public notice for this version was given, at least thirty days before `effectiveFrom` (D33 item 3). NULL, and required rather than optional, for the two cases where no notice period exists: the first adopted list, which nothing preceded, and a removal for cause, which takes effect at once. In an audit a missing key and an explicit null must not be distinguishable — the same reasoning `ct-segment.v1` gives its nullable `ref`.

adoptedAt.description: The date of the decision that adopted this version. Every addition and every removal is a board decision, minuted and published (D33 item 3).

decisionRef.description: The published minute of that decision.

standardUrl.description: Where the Recipient Standard itself is published (D33 item 2). Its minimum is constitutional and may only be tightened, so the text a reader checks a recipient against is a published document, not a paraphrase in a schema.

categories.description: The movement's seven published categories (statutes Art. 7; D33 item 1: the seven stay, and a 'category fund' is from now on nothing but the basket of listed recipients in that category). All seven are carried in every version, including one whose recipients have all been removed for cause, because the menu is the movement's and not the list's. EXACTLY ONE ENTRY PER SLUG, enforced: seven items, and one `contains` clause per slug of `$defs.categorySlug`. `uniqueItems` would not do this job — on an array of objects it compares whole objects, so seven entries all slugged `health` with distinct names would pass it, and a published version could claim seven categories while six of the movement's seven were silently absent.

fundId.description: The `cat-{slug}` form the ledger's `categoryFundId` carries, recorded so the two vocabularies resolve to each other without a lookup table.

recipients.description: The listed organisations. Ten to fifteen when the list is settled (D33 item 1) — not enforced here, because a removal for cause takes effect at once and the published state must remain expressible. Each entry carries its own Recipient Standard evidence and the category it is assigned to.

shareRule.description: How a category's amount for a month is divided among the listed recipients OF THAT CATEGORY. PROPOSED, NOT DECIDED: the default recorded here is equal shares per listed recipient, apportioned by largest remainder with ties broken by list order [OPERATOR: confirm]. It is published as a proposal so that no consumer mistakes it for a ruling — an undecided question is an open row of the record (URS §21), never a resolution invented in a schema. Note what this rule is NOT: it does not touch how much each CATEGORY receives (that is the allocation rule of FS-07 — payer declarations, the commons slice and the routing hierarchy), and it does not touch the annual cap on direct costs, which URS §21 OPEN-05 owns.

mode.description: `equal-per-recipient-in-category`: every listed recipient of a category carries the same share of that category's amount, which is what the sample dataset already assumes. One value today; a second value is added only by a recorded decision.

rounding.description: Largest remainder, the contract set's only apportionment rule (FS-07 FS07-030): quotas, then floors, then the remaining minor units one each in descending fractional-remainder order. Exactness holds by construction — the shares sum to the category's amount and no sub-centime dust exists.

tiebreak.description: The stated ascending stable key FS07-030 requires: the order of `recipients[]` in this published version. Publishing the tiebreak is what makes the apportionment reproducible by a reader rather than merely correct.

status.description: `proposed` until the operator confirms the rule; the value is part of the artifact so a page can say which it is. It flips to `decided` only when a dated decision says so.

note.description: The published wording of the rule, and what happens to a removed recipient's share for the month it was removed in: it goes to the other recipients of its category (D33 item 3).
Version-level narrative — what changed against the previous version and why, in the words a reader can check against the published minute.

categorySlug.description: The movement's seven published public-benefit categories (statutes Art. 7; ops decision D33 item 1). THIS IS THE ONE FILE IN THE CONTRACT SET THAT ENUMERATES THE MENU. Every schema here must validate on its own after a single download, so none may `$ref` another; the other fields carrying the same vocabulary constrain it by pattern and name this file, rather than repeating the enum and forking it at the next amendment. Those pointers exist today on `ledger-row.v1.categoryFundId`, `ledger-export.v1`'s export-row `categoryFundId` and `cost-support.v1.transfers[].category`. `purpose-yml.v1`'s own `categorySlug` does NOT yet carry one: it predates this menu, still describes '5–8 funds' and offers `climate` as an example, which is not one of the seven — aligning it belongs to the category-menu work and is deliberately not done here. A category that is not on this list would be a fabricated fact about where money goes: free-text categories and free-text recipients are forbidden outright.

recipientId.description: Platform-minted ULID, `rcp_` prefix, lowercase Crockford base32 — the same identifier the ledger's `disburse` rows and the cost-support transfers carry. It is minted once and never reused, so a removed recipient's history stays resolvable forever.

name.description: The organisation's registered name, as published. Money rows name organisations, never persons (URS ENG-083).

country.description: The country of registration as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. A code rather than a name because the two facts that hang on it are jurisdictional: whether the organisation may lawfully receive funds from a Swiss association under its own law (D33 item 2(b)), and which sanctions regimes the screening must clear. The rendering surface prints the country's name from the code.

category.description: The one category of the seven this organisation is assigned to (D33 item 1). One category per recipient: a basket is made of recipients, not of shares of a recipient.

shareBps.description: This recipient's share OF ITS CATEGORY's amount, in basis points. The shares of one category's active recipients sum to exactly 10000 — apportioned by the same largest-remainder rule with the same list-order tiebreak, so three equal recipients read 3333 / 3333 / 3334 rather than three rounded thirds that lose a unit. JSON Schema cannot express a sum across items, so the bound is stated here rather than left as a surprise, exactly as `purpose-yml.v1` states its micro-share bound. Zero is valid for a recipient that is listed but not yet active.

address.description: The organisation's published postal address (D33 item 2(g)). Required, because reachability is part of the Standard rather than a nicety.

registrationRef.description: The reference of the register entry that proves the organisation is a legally registered non-profit or charity in its country (D33 item 2(a)) — the register's own identifier, so a reader can open it.

standard.description: The Recipient Standard evidence held in the recipient file (D33 item 2). The Association keeps one file per recipient — registration, accounts, foreign-funding evidence, screening records, grant letter, receipts — and publishes its non-personal parts; these are the references into it.

accountsYears.description: Years of published accounts, independently audited or officially filed. The Standard's minimum of three is the schema's minimum (D33 item 2(a)): a shorter history is not a listing this contract can express.

foreignReceiptEvidence.description: The evidence that the organisation may lawfully receive funds from a Swiss association under its own country's law — for instance a foreign-contribution registration (D33 item 2(b)). One foreign-funding regime per recipient country is a cost the decision accepted with its eyes open.

screening.description: The sanctions screening records (D33 item 2(c)): the SECO, EU, UN and OFAC lists, checked before listing and again before every transfer, each check recorded. All four lists appear — hence at least four entries — and the array grows with every later check rather than being overwritten.

result.description: A `hit` is a removal for cause under D33 item 3: it takes effect at once, is published with its ground, and the entry carries `removedAt` and `removalGround`. The value exists in the enum because a screening result that cannot be recorded is a screening nobody can audit.

ref.description: The recorded check in the recipient file.

independenceDeclared.description: The declaration required by D33 item 2(d): no member, officer, board member, employee, contributor or repository owner of the Association is among the organisation's officers, and no financial link exists to any of them. Enforced as a constant because a listing without the declaration is not a listing the Standard permits; where a link does exist, the person is excluded from the vote (Art. 68 ZGB) and the fact is published in `declaredConflict`.

declaredConflict.description: The published fact where a link exists, together with the exclusion it caused (D33 item 2(d)).

bankTransferOnly.description: D33 item 2(e): paid by bank transfer only, never in cash and never in crypto-assets. A constant, because this is not a per-recipient preference — it is the payment rail the Standard allows.

grantLetterRef.description: The one-page grant letter stating the unrestricted purpose within the organisation's category, which the organisation accepts (D33 item 2(f)).

annualStatementRef.description: The short annual use-of-funds statement, or the published annual report that suffices for it (D33 item 2(f)).

receiptsRef.description: Where the per-transfer receipts are held. The receipt for one transfer travels on that transfer's own row (`cost-support.v1`).

activeFrom.description: The first month this recipient receives under. Additions are prospective, after thirty days' public notice (D33 item 3).

activeTo.description: The last month this recipient receives under, once an end is known. Absent means active with no end recorded.

removedAt.description: When a removal for cause took effect — at once, not at a month boundary (D33 item 3).

removalGround.description: The published ground for a removal for cause: a sanctions hit, loss of registration, failure to report. Published WITH the removal — a recipient that disappears without a stated ground is exactly the fact this list exists to prevent. The removed recipient's share for that month goes to the other recipients of its category, and nothing is ever clawed back from what was already transferred (D33 items 3 and 4).

sample.description: True in a sample dataset, on every entry, alongside a name that says so. A production list carries no `sample` entry: sample data is labelled sample, and no surface renders a fixture as a listed organisation.
